tendencies.text: Start from cala_facts and the user's own fields; use web research to confirm them or fill gaps, and cite the page you read.
A field you cannot support is null. Mark a field inferred only when it follows from cited facts (e.g. sectors from the product description).
When as_of is given, ignore every fact dated after it, including web pages about later rounds.
On an update, keep every field the update and new evidence do not touch exactly as it was; never drop a sourced field without a change entry that says why.
Rate each part from evidence: fit (clarity of sector and stage), traction (rounds, customers), team, activity (recent rounds or leads); total is the mean of the parts.

Make each cala_facts row a dataset fact with its own id, and copy its fields verbatim into the quote. Never turn 'Not disclosed' investors into a named investor, and never make a year-only date like '2025' more precise. If the data is too thin for a field, set it to null rather than guess.

Before using a web fact, confirm it is the same company. A matching name isn't enough: the domain and country/sector must also agree with cala_facts. If they conflict, keep the dataset value and drop the web claim. Take website from the company's own domain, and give each web fact a url, a short verbatim quote and a date.

Map stage to the standard ladder (pre-seed, seed, series_a, ...) using the latest round's reported label, not its size. If the size looks wrong for the label (e.g. a $100M+ seed), keep the label and note it. Set sources to inferred: true for any stage or sector you derived rather than read.

For investors, count a round as led only if the investor is explicitly named as lead (the one who sets the terms and usually writes the largest check). lead_share = rounds led / rounds participated in, from cited rounds only. last_lead_date = the date of the latest led round. With no lead data, set both to null, not 0.

Score each rating part from cited facts: traction from round size and recency, activity from deal count and last lead date. Score team only if a fact supports it. Total = mean of the scored parts, and keep scores near 0.5 when evidence is thin. When revising, change only what the update or new facts support, and log field, old, new and reason.

notes: Drafted by the training research step from web search. Not validated.
